children: Macquarie says Australia's new domestic natural-gas reservation policy doesn't appear problematic for the Australia Pacific LNG project, which is part owned by Origin Energy. That view reflect APLNG's large domestic production. Still, Macquarie does highlight the threat of a potential fall in natural-gas prices to A$10-A$11 per gigajoule, from A$12-A$13/GJ. "Origin is exposed via its low cost APLNG contract (40 petajoules), and the reset of the Beach contact which will be mispriced, relative to forward prices," says Macquarie. It estimates some A$60 million of Ebitda is at risk. Macquarie retains a neutral call on Origin. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
